title: AppRouter has zero RoleGuard wrappers — admin/internal routes accessible to any authenticated user
detail: AppRouter.jsx defines ~30 routes and not a single one is wrapped in <RoleGuard>. Admin-only paths (/admin, /flow-monitor, /send-queue, /absorption, /capital-plan) and internal-tool paths (/nora, /interview) are reachable by typing the URL hash, regardless of user role. The RoleGuard component exists in shared modules and is correctly built (RoleGuard.jsx); it's just never used in the router. NavPanel hides nav items via the nav_menu_{role} config pattern, but a user who knows the URL can bypass that entirely. For external customer-facing user testing, an external tester landing on /#/admin would see admin actions. Per CR-2026-04-09-0220, NavPanel ALSO doesn't role-gate properly — the two issues compound.
evidence: AppRouter.jsx:56-151 — every Route uses bare element prop, no RoleGuard imports. Compare to the existence of src/RoleGuard.jsx (which exports the component) and the JS-06/C-06 rule documented in usePortalUser.jsx:9 ('Actions the user cannot perform are REMOVED FROM THE DOM entirely').
recommendedFix: Wrap admin/internal routes in <RoleGuard require="admin">: e.g. `<Route path="admin" element={<RoleGuard require="admin" fallback={<Navigate to="/dashboard" replace />}><Admin /></RoleGuard>} />`. Apply to /admin, /flow-monitor, /send-queue, /absorption, /capital-plan minimum. The fallback should redirect non-admins to /dashboard rather than render null (otherwise the user sees a blank page with no explanation). Same pattern for manager-only routes (e.g. /onboarding/:id depending on rule). This is a coordinated change with CR-2026-04-09-0220 (NavPanel role logic).
